sections.purpose: To prepare thin uniform sections of plant tissue, embedded specimens, or paraffin blocks for microscopic examination in pharmacognosy and histology practicals.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for preparation of transverse sections (T.S.) and longitudinal sections (L.S.) of plant materials for identification and histological studies.
procedure: Ensure the microtome blade is sharp and securely clamped in the blade holder — use appropriate blade type (rotary or sledge microtome).
Fix the tissue block (paraffin-embedded or hand-sectioning tissue) securely in the specimen clamp.
Set the desired section thickness using the micrometer dial: for plant tissues 10–15 µm is typical; for general histology 5–10 µm.
Advance the specimen slowly toward the blade using the coarse advance wheel to trim the block face until a full section is obtained.
Rotate the handwheel of the rotary microtome steadily and evenly to cut a ribbon of sections.
Use a fine brush to guide the ribbon off the blade and transfer to a water bath at 40–45°C to allow sections to flatten.
Lift the section from the warm water bath using a glass slide, positioning the section centrally.
Drain excess water and place slides on a slide warmer (37–40°C) to allow sections to adhere and dry for at least 30 minutes.
For hand sections of fresh plant tissue: Use a sharp razor blade to cut free-hand sections as thin as possible, then transfer to a watch glass with water.
Transfer sections to staining solutions (e.g., safranin for cell walls, alcian blue for mucilage) as per staining protocol.
Mount stained sections in glycerine or DPX mounting medium and apply a coverslip.
Allow mounting medium to set before viewing under microscope.
Label all slides with material, staining method, section type, and date.
Clean the microtome blade area with a soft brush to remove wax residue after sectioning.
precautions: Exercise extreme caution when handling and changing microtome blades — blades are razor sharp.
Use blade-handling forceps or blade removal tools — never touch the cutting edge with bare fingers.
Lock the specimen holder and engage the blade safety mechanism before adjusting blade or specimen.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling blades and mounting them into the holder.
Keep fingers away from the cutting path at all times during operation.
Ensure the microtome is placed on a stable, vibration-free surface for thin sections.
Dispose of used blades in a sharps container — never in general waste.
Keep the water bath temperature controlled — too hot causes sections to disintegrate.
Lubricate the microtome moving parts as per manufacturer's maintenance schedule.
